answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. Consider a harbor as the anchor of the cost. A echo stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a vertex holds...
